title: Migration remains a development asset under pressure from disruption, displacement, climate mobility, and constrained pathways
source_unit: International Organization for Migration, World Migration Report 2026
geography: Global migration, mobility, displacement, migrant development contributions, climate mobility, regular pathways, and community response

observations.period: mid-2024; international migration and mobility frame

denominator.unit: global population, international migrant stock, and migration-mobility frame

international_migrants_mid_2024.unit: millions of international migrants worldwide by mid-2024

cross_border_movement.value: cross-border movement remains the exception rather than the norm, while internal migration is more common

work_channel.value: work is the main reason among people who migrate internationally, and migrant workers constitute the majority

observations.method: IOM compilation and synthesis of global migration stocks, flows, migrant-group, labor, and mobility evidence.
observations.uncertainty: International migrant stocks are estimates rather than complete movement histories; reasons for migration and migrant-worker classifications vary across countries and data systems.
observations.subgroup: International migrants, migrant workers, students, refugees, asylum-seekers, internally displaced people, origin communities, and destination institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Most people remain in their country of birth, and migration can be temporary, circular, internal, or locally embedded rather than a one-way international move.

internal_displacement.unit: more than millions of people living in internal displacement globally by the end of 2024

disruption_channels.value: geopolitical tensions, conflict, environmental disruption, and distortion of facts are reshaping migration and displacement

response_problem.value: displacement responses must connect protection, durable solutions, local capacity, and mobility governance

observations.method: IOM synthesis of displacement tracking, conflict and environmental context, and migration-governance analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Displacement counts depend on reporting, definitions, duration, and access; the aggregate stock does not measure individual safety, intention to return, or service quality.
observations.subgroup: Internally displaced people, refugees, host communities, local authorities, humanitarian organizations, and populations exposed to conflict or environmental shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Displacement can decline through return, resettlement, integration, or under-reporting; a stock change alone does not identify whether conditions improved.

observations.period: 2026; migration as development infrastructure under pressure

denominator.unit: migration-development, remittance, investment, skills, and civic-engagement frame

development_contributions.value: migrants and diasporas contribute through remittances, investment, knowledge and skills transfer, and civic and political engagement

strategic_asset_at_risk.value: migration is treated as a strategic development asset increasingly exposed to disruption and policy risk

policy_question.value: protecting development gains requires attention to financing, regular pathways, rights, and institutional capacity

observations.method: IOM thematic analysis of migration-development linkages, remittances, investment, skills, civic engagement, and global financing frameworks.
observations.uncertainty: Sector-level development contributions are heterogeneous and do not establish that migration causes aggregate development outcomes or that benefits reach all origin and destination communities.
observations.subgroup: Migrants, diasporas, origin households and communities, destination economies, employers, public institutions, and financial-transfer systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Remittances and skills transfer can support resilience, but migration can also impose care gaps, recruitment costs, brain drain, exclusion, or dependence on external income.

observations.period: 2026; climate mobility, regular pathways, disability, and local action

denominator.unit: IOM thematic chapters on climate mobility, pathways, disability, and community response

climate_mobility.value: environmental disruption is a central feature of contemporary mobility and requires local and community action

regular_pathways.value: regular migration pathways require policy designs that distinguish myths, realities, opportunities, and protection needs

inclusion.value: disability and migration require explicit attention to distinct risks, access, and response capacity

observations.method: IOM thematic synthesis of climate mobility, regular migration pathways, internal displacement, disability and migration, and local/community responses.
observations.uncertainty: The thematic chapters identify mechanisms and policy questions rather than estimating individual climate-migration decisions, causal pathway effects, or universal local outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Climate-affected communities, migrants with disabilities, displaced people, local governments, community organizations, employers, and pathway administrators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Environmental stress does not mechanically produce migration; local adaptation, livelihoods, social networks, infrastructure, and public choices shape whether people move, stay, or return.

related_sources.claim: IOM Chapter 2 provides the global migrant-stock, migrant-group, displacement, and remittance evidence base.
IOM Chapter 4 provides complementary migration-development, remittance, investment, skills, and civic-engagement analysis.

boundary: This record adds a global migration, displacement, development, climate-mobility, pathway, disability, and local-response route. It uses aggregate stocks, report synthesis, and thematic policy analysis, not individual migration histories, respondent-level attitudes, causal remittance or pathway estimates, or a claim that climate stress mechanically causes migration.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IOM World Migration Report 2026 materials were reviewed for the global migrant stock, internal displacement, migration-development contributions, disruption, regular pathways, climate mobility, disability, and community-action chapters.
